…

# sc-back-link

The "Back" control: a 44px glass pill with a back chevron, at the start of `sc-app-bar` or above the question on a form page.

## Usage

```html
<!-- Preferred: the previous page has a URL, so it works without JavaScript. -->
<sc-back-link href="/renew/vehicle"></sc-back-link>

<!-- In a single-page app: a <button>; handle click in your router. -->
<sc-back-link id="back"></sc-back-link>
<script>document.getElementById('back').addEventListener('click', () => history.back());</script>
```

- Use it on every step of a journey except the first. It goes to the previous step, not the start of the service.
- With `href` it renders an `<a>`; without it, a `<button type="button">`. Prefer `href`: it keeps the browser's own behaviour (open in new tab, status bar URL).
- The label defaults to "Back" / "رجوع" in the page language. Override it with the default slot only when "Back" would be unclear: `<sc-back-link href="/vehicles">Back to my vehicles</sc-back-link>`.
- `appearance="glass"` (default) is for the app bar and channel washes. Use `appearance="plain"` inside a page body on a solid surface.

### Arabic

The chevron mirrors, so it points right, toward the start of the line, and sits on the right of the label.

### Accessibility

The accessible name is the label ("Back"). Keyboard: Tab to it, Enter follows the link; Space also activates the button form. It delegates focus, so `el.focus()` focuses the inner control. Under `prefers-reduced-transparency` the glass becomes a solid surface; in forced colours it gets a system-coloured border.

### Styling hooks

Parts: `control`, `label`, `icon`.

# sc-button

Starts an action. If it goes somewhere instead, use `sc-link` (or `sc-button href` for a call to action that must look like a button, such as "Start now").

## Usage

```html
<sc-button type="submit" icon="arrow-forward">Continue</sc-button>
<sc-button variant="secondary">Save and finish later</sc-button>
<sc-button href="/renew/start" icon="arrow-forward">Start now</sc-button>
```

### Which variant

| Variant | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | The one main action on the page. Never more than one per page or section. | "Continue", "Pay with Dubai Pay" |
| `secondary` | Other actions next to a primary one, or the main action when it isn't the way forward. | "Save and finish later", "Change" |
| `tertiary` | Low-emphasis actions that would compete with the primary if they had a fill. | "Cancel", "View all services" |
| `destructive` | An action that deletes data or can't be undone. Confirm it on the next screen. | "Delete draft", "Cancel renewal" |
| `handoff` | A shared government hand-off. City indigo on every channel, so it never looks like the channel's own action (U3). | "Sign in with UAE PASS", "Pay with Dubai Pay" |

- Heights follow the variant: 56px for `primary`, `destructive` and `handoff`; 48px for `secondary` and `tertiary`. Set `size="l"` (56px) or `size="m"` (48px) to override; `size="xl"` (64px) is for the hero search only.
- Use `full-width` on narrow screens when the button ends a form.
- Put the primary button first in the reading order. In Arabic it sits on the right automatically.

### Content

- Start with a verb and say what happens: "Continue", "Pay with Dubai Pay", "Save and finish later". Not "Submit", "OK" or "Click here".
- Sentence case, no full stop, as short as it can be while staying specific. Write the Arabic label, don't machine-translate it.
- Use the `arrow-forward` icon at the end only for actions that move the user forward in a journey. It mirrors in Arabic. Don't add icons for decoration.
- Amounts and references inside a label stay left-to-right: `<sc-button>Pay <sc-ltr>AED 450.00</sc-ltr></sc-button>`.

### States

- **Loading:** set `loading` while the action runs (for example, while a payment starts). The button keeps its width, shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, announces "Pay with Dubai Pay, Loading" (or the Arabic equivalent) and ignores clicks. Remove `loading` when the action ends.
- **Disabled:** supported, but avoid it. A disabled button can't be focused and gives no reason, so many users can't tell why they're stuck. Leave it enabled and show an error message (and `sc-error-summary`) when the user tries to continue.

### Forms

`sc-button` renders a native `<button>` (or `<a>`) in light DOM (v2, decision A2), so it is a real form control:

- `type="submit"` submits the surrounding `<form>`, and the first submit button is the form's **default button**: Enter in any field submits through it. `name`, `value` and `form="<form id>"` work as on a native button. `type="reset"` resets the form. The default `type` is `button`, unlike the native element.
- A `<fieldset disabled>` disables it natively.
- `focus()` and `click()` on the host reach the native control.
- There is no `::part()` in v2. Style overrides, if you must, target `.sc-button`, `.sc-button__label` and `.sc-button__icon`; the component's rules are in `@layer sc.components`, so your unlayered CSS wins.
- Frameworks that own children (React) must not re-render the label text after upgrade: Stencil moves it into the native button.

# sc-callout

An important message inside the page content: something the user must know before they act, or the result of what they just did. If the message is about errors in the user's answers, use `sc-error-summary` and field errors instead. If it's the status of a task or payment in a list, use `sc-status-tag`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-callout tone="warning">
  If your payment is interrupted, don't pay again. Check the payment status in My tasks first.
</sc-callout>

<sc-callout tone="success" heading="Registration renewed" heading-level="2">
  Your vehicle registration is valid until 18 October 2027.
</sc-callout>
```

### Which tone

| Tone | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `info` (default) | Guidance the user needs. Neutral fill, ink icon. | "You'll need your plate number and Emirates ID number." |
| `success` | Something worked. | "We've sent the receipt to your email." |
| `warning` | Something the user must know to avoid a problem. | "If your payment is interrupted, don't pay again…" |
| `error` | Something went wrong that isn't about their answers. | "Your payment didn't go through. No money has been taken." |

Each tone has its own fill, its own icon and a visually hidden word read before the message ("Warning:" / "تنبيه:"), so the meaning never relies on colour. Override the word with `tone-label` if a different one fits better.

### Content

- One callout per section at most; if everything is highlighted, nothing is.
- Lead with what the user should do or know. Short sentences, sentence case. Write the Arabic, don't translate word for word.
- `heading` is optional bold text. It is a plain paragraph by default; set `heading-level` (2–6) only when the heading belongs in the page outline. Use the `heading` slot for rich content.
- Inline links and `<sc-ltr>` for amounts and references are fine in the message.
- It isn't a live region. If you insert one after the page loads (for example after a payment check), wrap it in an element with `role="status"` or move focus to it.

### Styling hooks

Parts: `container`, `icon`, `heading`, `content`.

# sc-card A surface for grouping related content: a life event and its steps, a task, a section of answers. If the whole box is a link to a service, use `sc-service-card` instead; for "Check your answers", `sc-summary-list` draws its own card. ## Usage ```html

My tasks

Set `landmark="section"` only for a part of the page users would want to jump to ("My tasks"), and `landmark="article"` for self-contained content such as a news item. The fill, radius and shadow come from tokens and follow light and dark themes; in forced colours the card keeps a visible edge.

# sc-channel-chip

Points to another channel that also offers this service: "Also on Dubai Transport". It is the one component that names a channel: it sets `data-channel` on itself, so it always shows that channel's subtle and ink colours, whatever channel the page is in.

## Usage

```html
<!-- A label -->
<sc-channel-chip channel="transport"></sc-channel-chip>

<!-- A link to the service on that channel -->
<sc-channel-chip channel="transport" href="https://transport.dubai.gov.ae/renew"></sc-channel-chip>
```

`channel` is one of `now`, `transport`, `visit`, `justice`, `build`, `invest`, `trade`.

### Content

- The text comes from strings: "Also on {channel}" / "متوفر أيضًا في {channel}", with the channel's own name. Override it with `label` or the default slot only when the chip says something more specific ("Pay fines on Dubai Justice"), and always name the channel.
- Use it on service cards and service start pages, never as the main way forward.

### Link

With `href` it renders an `<a>` with an end chevron (mirrored in Arabic). The pill stays compact (about 30px) but its hit area grows to 44px without moving the layout; leave a little space above and below it. Without `href` it isn't focusable.

### Styling hooks

Parts: `chip`, `dot`, `icon` (links only).

# sc-checkbox

A checkbox: an option in `sc-checkbox-group`, or one box on its own for a single statement people must confirm, such as "I confirm the vehicle details are correct".

## Usage

```html
<sc-checkbox name="confirm" value="yes" required>I confirm the vehicle details are correct</sc-checkbox>
```

- The content is the label. Keep it short; put detail in `hint` (or the `hint` slot).
- 24px box inside a 44px target: the whole label row is clickable. Space toggles it. The tick is a symbol, so it never mirrors in Arabic.
- **On its own:** `error` shows the error bar, the message with "Error:" and `aria-invalid`. `required` reports `valueMissing` until it's checked.
- **In a group:** the group shows the error and passes it down; the box submits its `value` under the group's `name` unless it has its own `name`.
- Form-associated: submits `value` (default `on`) when checked, resets to its initial `checked`, follows `<fieldset disabled>`. `change` is re-dispatched on the host and `scChange` carries `{ checked, value }`.

# sc-checkbox-group

Several choices from a short list: "Which documents do you have?", "Send reminders by". Use `sc-radio-group` when only one answer is allowed. For a single yes/no statement ("I confirm the vehicle details are correct") use one `sc-checkbox` on its own.

## Usage

```html
<sc-checkbox-group name="documents" label="Which documents do you have?" hint="Select all that apply">
  <sc-checkbox value="insurance">Valid insurance policy</sc-checkbox>
  <sc-checkbox value="inspection" hint="From a centre approved by RTA">Technical inspection certificate</sc-checkbox>
  <sc-checkbox value="fines">Receipt for paid fines</sc-checkbox>
</sc-checkbox-group>
```

- Legend, hint, `optional`, `error`, `inline`, `heading-level` and `disabled` work as in `sc-radio-group`.
- Say "Select all that apply" in the hint. Order options logically; don't pre-check options for people.
- **Error:** set `error` on the group. The group shows the bar and message; every box gets the error border and `aria-invalid`. The boxes' own `error` is ignored inside a group.

### How it stays accessible across shadow roots

Unlike radios, checkboxes don't need to share a tree: each one is independent (its own Tab stop, Space toggles it). So each `sc-checkbox` keeps its own native `<input type="checkbox">`, `<label>` and hint in **its own shadow root**, which also lets it work on its own. The group renders the `<fieldset>`, `<legend>`, hint and error in its shadow root and slots the checkboxes inside the fieldset. The accessibility tree follows the flattened tree, so screen readers find the checkboxes inside the group named by the legend and described by the hint and error. The group passes its error and disabled state down to each box.

Tested in `sc-checkbox-group.e2e.ts` against Chromium's accessibility tree (group name and description, checkbox names inside the group), with the keyboard (Tab to each box, Space toggles) and axe in English and Arabic, light and dark.

### Forms

Each checked box submits its own `value` under the group's `name` (or its own `name`), so the form data is `documents=insurance&documents=fines`, as with native checkboxes. Reset restores each box. The group is form-associated only to report `valueMissing` when `required` and nothing is checked. `scGroupChange` carries `{ value: string[] }`, the checked values.

# sc-date-input

A date people know: a date of birth, the start date on an insurance policy, the date a vehicle was exported. Don't use it for a date people need to pick from a calendar (an appointment): that needs a date picker.

## Usage

```html
<sc-date-input
  name="insuranceStart"
  label="When does your insurance policy start?"
  hint="For example, 27 3 2026"
></sc-date-input>
```

- Three labelled boxes, Day, Month and Year (يوم / شهر / سنة), in a `<fieldset>` with the question as the `<legend>`. Each box uses the numeric keyboard (`inputmode="numeric"`).
- **In Arabic** the boxes run right to left: Day on the right, Year on the left. Digits stay Latin.
- **Hint:** give an example in the order of the boxes: "For example, 27 3 2026".
- **Error on one part:** set `error` and `error-parts` to the boxes it's about, for example `error-parts="year"` with "The date your policy starts must include a year". Only those boxes get the error border and `aria-invalid`. Without `error-parts`, the error highlights all three.
- **Date of birth:** `autocomplete="bday"` sets `bday-day`, `bday-month`, `bday-year` on the boxes.
- `optional`, `heading-level` and `disabled` work as in the other fields.

### Value and forms

- `value` is an ISO date (`2026-03-27`). It's empty while the boxes don't make a real date (31 April, a 2-digit year). Setting `value` fills the boxes.
- The form gets the ISO date under `name`, plus the raw parts as `name-day`, `name-month` and `name-year`, so the server can validate and re-display exactly what was typed.
- Validity: `valueMissing` when `required` and every box is empty; `badInput` ("The date must be a real date") when something is typed but it isn't a real date. Reset restores the initial `value`.
- `scInput` and `scChange` carry `{ value, day, month, year }`. The host delegates focus to the Day box, so an error summary can focus the field by its `id`.

# sc-date-range

A start and an end date that relate to a calendar: filtering payments or fines between two dates, the nights of a stay on Visit Dubai, how long a permit lasts. For a single date people already know (a date of birth, a policy start date), use `sc-date-input`: people type those faster than they find them in a calendar.

## Usage

```html
<sc-date-range
  name="payments"
  label="Show payments between"
  hint="For example, 21 9 2026"
  start="2026-09-21"
  end="2026-10-09"
  max="2026-10-19"
  max-days="365"
  presets
></sc-date-range>
```

- **Field:** a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, the hint, then one 54px frame with two typed segments, From and To (من / إلى), an arrow between them (→, ← in Arabic) and a calendar button at inline-end. People can always type: "21/9/2026", "21 9 2026" and "21-09-2026" all work, and each segment is formatted on blur ("21 Sep 2026").
- **Picker:** the calendar button opens a popover on medium and wider screens: one or two months (`months`, `auto` shows two from 720px), always 6 weeks, Monday first, and optional presets at inline-start. The first click sets the start, the second the end; a day before the start, or any day after a complete range, starts again. Apply writes both dates, closes the picker and returns focus to the button; Escape or a click outside closes without changes. Below 600px it is a modal bottom sheet with From / To chips, preset chips and a scrolling list of months; it can be dragged down to close.
- **Presets:** `presets` shows Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month and This year (clamped to `min` / `max`). Pass a JSON list to replace them, for a booking calendar: `[{"label": "This weekend", "start": "2026-10-24", "end": "2026-10-25"}]`. A preset applies at once and doesn't close the picker.
- **Limits:** `min` and `max` disable days outside them (for payment filters, `max` is today); `min-days` and `max-days` disable days that would make the range too short or too long once a start is chosen, and the footer says "You can choose up to 90 days".
- **Keyboard** (ARIA APG date picker): arrows move a day and move visually, so in Arabic Left is the next day; Up and Down move a week; Home and End go to the start and end of the week; Page Up / Page Down change the month and Shift with them the year; Enter or Space chooses the day. Keyboard month changes are instant; pointer ones crossfade.
- **Errors:** set `error` and `error-parts` (`start`, `end` or `both`) as on the other fields. The component also shows its own message on blur for an impossible range (end before start, a date that isn't real, outside `min`/`max`, too long or too short) and never swaps the dates; "Enter a start date" and "Enter an end date" wait for a submit.
- **Forms:** submits `name-start` and `name-end` as ISO dates (empty until each is a real date) and resets to the initial range. Validity: `valueMissing` (with `required`, or a half-filled range), `badInput`, `rangeUnderflow`, `rangeOverflow`. `scChange` carries `{ start, end }`; `scOpen` and `scClose` fire with the picker. Methods: `open()`, `close()`, `setFocus()`.
- **Today:** the `today` property fixes "today" (ISO) when the server's date matters, and in tests.
- **Arabic:** the whole component mirrors: From is on the right, Monday is the rightmost column, the previous-month button is on the right and presets sit on the right. Month and weekday names are Arabic, digits stay Latin. Gregorian only for now.

# sc-error-summary Lists every error on the page after the user submits a form, so they can see all the problems at once and jump to each field. Use it with the field's own error message: the summary never replaces it. Don't use it for problems that aren't about the user's answers (a failed payment, a service that's down): use `sc-callout tone="error"` for those. ## Usage ```html
Enter the plate code Enter the plate number using numbers only, like 12345

What is your plate number?

…
``` Or from JavaScript, after client-side validation: ```js const summary = document.querySelector('sc-error-summary'); summary.errors = [{ href: '#plate-number', text: 'Enter the plate number using numbers only, like 12345' }]; ``` ### Placement and behaviour - Put it at the top of `
`, above the `

`, and only when there are errors. With no items it hides itself. - When it first has errors (on page load, or when `errors` goes from empty to filled) it moves focus to itself (`tabindex="-1"`), so screen readers read the heading and every error straight away. It deliberately has no `role="alert"`: the focus move is the announcement, and a live region as well can make screen readers read the summary twice. The focused box is a group named by its heading (`aria-labelledby`). Don't move focus anywhere else on that page load. Use `no-autofocus` only if you move focus yourself with `setFocus()`. - Add "Error: " to the start of the page `` too. - Following a link moves focus to the field and scrolls it into view, without changing the URL. It works with a plain `<input id>` and with field components (`sc-text-input`, `sc-date-input` …) that delegate focus to their inner control, and finds the target in the summary's own shadow root first, then in the document. - Slotted links are read from the light DOM (directly, or inside a `<ul>`) and rendered as a list inside the component; the list updates when they change. The `errors` property wins when it is set and not empty. ### Content - Each item is the same message as the one shown next to the field, in the same order as the fields on the page. - Link to the field's `id`, not to the label. For a date, link to the first part with a problem. - The heading is "There is a problem" / "توجد مشكلة". Change it (`heading`) only when a more specific heading helps, e.g. "Check your vehicle details". Use the `description` slot for one short sentence when the errors need context. - In Arabic, keep plates and numbers left-to-right inside the message: `يُرجى إدخال رقم اللوحة بالأرقام فقط، مثل <bdi dir="ltr">12345</bdi>`. ### Styling hooks Parts: `container`, `heading`, `list`. The border and links use the error colour; the focus ring uses the channel action colour.

# sc-search

A search box for a channel or a list of services.

## Usage

```html
<sc-search label="Search Dubai Now services" placeholder="Try “renew car registration” or “school fees”" action="/search"></sc-search>
```

```js
document.querySelector('sc-search').addEventListener('scSearch', (ev) => {
  ev.preventDefault();            // handle it in the page instead of going to `action`
  showResults(ev.detail.value);
});
```

- Give it a specific `label` ("Search Dubai Now services"). Hide it visually with `label-hidden` only where the context makes the purpose obvious, such as a hero that asks "What do you need to do?"; screen readers still read it.

One choice from a list that's too long for radios, such as the issuing authority of a plate or an inspection centre. Use `sc-radio-group` when there are about 7 options or fewer: radios show every option without opening anything. # sc-spinner

Shows that something is loading: inline, 20px, in the current text colour. Inside a button, use `sc-button loading` instead. For a whole page, prefer showing content as soon as you can.

## Usage

# sc-status-tag

The status of a task, application or payment, usually in a list or next to a heading: "Paid", "Action needed", "In review", "Expires in 15 days". For a message the user must read, use `sc-callout`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-status-tag tone="error">Action needed</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag tone="success">Paid</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag tone="warning">Expires in 15 days</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag>In review</sc-status-tag>
```

### Which tone

| Tone | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `neutral` (default) | A plain state with nothing to do yet: "Draft", "In review". |
| `success` | Done: "Paid", "Approved", "Completed". |
| `warning` | Needs attention soon: "Expires in 15 days". |
| `error` | Blocked or failed: "Action needed", "Payment failed". |
| `channel` | Deprecated: not a status in the vocabulary below. It logs a console warning and will be removed in the next major version. |

### Status words

Services show only the status words in the standard's status vocabulary (chapter 9.6), each with its fixed tone. Arabic forms agree with the noun they describe; task statuses agree with "مهمة".

| Kind | Status | Arabic | Tone |
|---|---|---|---|
| Application | Draft | مسودة | `neutral` |
| Application | Received | تم الاستلام | `neutral` |
| Application | In review | قيد المراجعة | `neutral` |
| Application | Action needed | إجراء مطلوب | `error` |
| Application | Approved | تمت الموافقة | `success` |
| Application | Not approved | لم تتم الموافقة | `neutral` |
| Application | Completed | مكتمل | `success` |
| Application | Withdrawn | تم السحب | `neutral` |
| Application | Cancelled | تم الإلغاء | `neutral` |
| Application | Expires in {n} days | ينتهي خلال {n} يومًا | `warning` |
| Task | Not started | لم تبدأ | `neutral` |
| Task | In progress | قيد التنفيذ | `neutral` |
| Task | Completed | مكتملة | `success` |
| Task | Cannot start yet | غير متاحة بعد | `neutral` |
| Payment | Not paid | بانتظار الدفع | `warning` |
| Payment | Checking payment | جارٍ التحقق من الدفع | `neutral` |
| Payment | Paid | تم الدفع | `success` |
| Payment | Payment failed | تعذّر الدفع | `error` |
| Payment | Payment cancelled | تم إلغاء الدفع | `neutral` |
| Payment | Refund requested | تم طلب الاسترداد | `neutral` |
| Payment | Refund in progress | الاسترداد قيد التنفيذ | `neutral` |
| Payment | Refunded | تم الاسترداد | `success` |

"Paid" never stands for "Approved", and "Received" never stands for "Completed".

### Content

- Always write the status in words; the colour and dot only support them. Two or three words, sentence case, no full stop.
- Use the words in the table below, the same everywhere in a service.
- Digits stay Latin in Arabic ("ينتهي خلال 15 يومًا").
- Not interactive and not announced on change. If the status changes while the user is on the page, also announce it (for example with a `role="status"` region).

### Styling hooks

Parts: `tag`, `dot`.

# sc-step-progress

Shows where the user is in a short journey: "Step 2 of 4", the current step's name and a segmented track. Use it for linear journeys of 2 to about 7 question pages. Don't use it for long or branching journeys, where the total isn't known.

## Usage

```html
<sc-step-progress current="2" total="4" label="Plate number"></sc-step-progress>
```

- `current` is clamped between 1 and `total`.
- Override the wording with `count-text`, keeping the `{current}` and `{total}` placeholders.

### Content

- Count only the question pages: not the start page, "Check your answers" or the confirmation.
- `label` is the current step's short name, matching the page's heading in spirit ("Plate number", "Pay").

Parts: `meta`, `label`, `count`, `track`.

# sc-table A table compares rows of the same kind of thing across a few attributes: a person's fines, their payments, the status of their permit applications. Each row is one thing; each column is one attribute. For the details of one thing, use `sc-summary-list`. Never use a table for layout. ## Usage ```html
Reference Date Offence Status Amount
F-2026-118204 14 Mar 2026 Speeding: 21 to 30 km/h over the limit Not paid AED 600.00
Showing 1–20 of 1,284 fines …Previous / Next…
Pay 2 fines ``` - **Scoped, not shadowed.** The component styles and enhances your native ``, so screen readers announce rows, columns and headers. Write `th scope="col"` headers and a `th scope="row"` as each row's first cell; it usually carries the row's link. Whole rows are never clickable. - **Caption** is required: `caption` writes a native `
`. Use `caption-hidden` when a heading straight above says the same thing. - **Column types** go on the header cell as `data-type` and set alignment, wrapping and figures for the whole column: `text` (wraps, never truncated), `reference` (nowrap, tabular; wrap the value in `sc-ltr`), `date`, `amount` (end-aligned, nowrap: the column grows instead), `status` (an `sc-status-tag`), `action` (end-aligned). Digits are Latin in both languages. - **Missing values:** leave the cell empty and the component writes a muted "None" (لا يوجد). Never a bare dash. - **Sorting:** add `data-sort` (optionally with a column key, `data-sort="amount"`) to a header. It becomes a button; Enter or a click cycles ascending and descending, one column at a time, sets `aria-sort` and announces "Sorted by Amount, highest first". The component only emits `scSort` with `{ column, direction }`: sort the data in the service (usually on the server) and re-render the rows. Sorting is never animated. - **Selection:** `selectable` adds a checkbox column at inline-start, identified by `tr[data-id]`, and a selection bar with the count, the total of the amount column (from `data-value`, or the cell text) and your `actions` slot. Label the checkboxes with `strings` ("Select fine {row}"). `selection-label` takes plural forms separated by `|` (English one|other; Arabic zero|one|two|few|many|other). `tr[data-selected]` preselects a row. `scSelectionChange` carries `{ ids }`. - **States:** `loading` shows 5 skeleton rows at the real column widths (the header stays). With no rows, the `empty` slot replaces the table: a `title-s` sentence and an optional next step ("You have no fines"; never "No data"). Add `filtered` for "No results" after a filter, which keeps the header. Put an `sc-callout tone="error"` with a "Try again" button in the `error` slot when the data can't load. Counts in the footer follow plural rules: "Showing 1 fine", never "1–1 of 1". - **Density:** `compact` (44px rows) is for staff tools with long lists. - **Below 600px** (the component's own width), `responsive="stack"` (default, up to about 6 columns) turns rows into cards: the row header is the title, the status sits at top inline-end, other cells become label and value pairs, the amount is the last line in `title-m` and the action a full-width link row. `responsive="scroll"` keeps the table in a horizontal scroll region (focusable, named by the caption) with the row header sticky at inline-start and a shadow on the side with more content. A table wider than its container always scrolls rather than clipping. - **Links in cells** get a target of at least 44 × 44 px (an invisible hit area around the text) without changing the row height. - **Screen-reader context:** `class="sc-visually-hidden"` inside the table hides text visually: `View fine F-2026-118204`. - **Arabic:** everything mirrors: the first column and the checkboxes are on the right, amounts and actions align left, and the sort glyph sits after the label. Rows grow with the Arabic leading; nothing is fixed-height.

# sc-textarea

A longer answer that can run to several sentences: why a registration is being cancelled, a description of damage, a note for the inspector. For one line use `sc-text-input`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-textarea
  name="reason"
  label="Why are you cancelling the registration?"
  hint="For example, the vehicle was sold or exported"
  maxlength="200"
></sc-textarea>
```

Label, hint, `optional`, `error`, `required`, `heading-level`, form association and focus delegation work exactly as in `sc-text-input` (see its readme).

### Character count

Set `maxlength` to show a count under the box: "You have 120 characters remaining" / "يتبقى لديك 120 حرفًا".

- **Typing isn't cut off.** People can type past the limit (no native `maxlength`), then the count says "You have 6 characters too many" in the error colour, the box gets the error border and `aria-invalid`, and the field reports `tooLong`, so the form won't pass `checkValidity()`. Editing down is easier than finding out the end of your text was silently dropped.
- **Announced politely, after a pause.** The visible count changes on every keystroke but is hidden from screen readers. A separate polite live region (`aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic`) is updated once typing has paused for one second, so screen reader users hear the count when they stop, not on every key.
- **Described up front.** "You can enter up to 200 characters" is part of the textarea's description, so the limit is heard on focus.
- **Arabic plurals.** The Arabic count uses the right form for the number (حرف واحد، حرفان، 3 أحرف، 120 حرفًا، 100 حرف), chosen with `Intl.PluralRules('ar')`. Characters are counted as people see them, so an emoji counts as one.

Use a limit only when there is a real one (a system field length). Size the box with `rows` to fit a typical answer.
